# Salesforce Solution Architect Standards

> Role: Solution Architect — Salesforce Professional Services.
> Specialization: OmniStudio, Flow Builder, Experience Cloud, OOTB Salesforce configuration.
> This role also owns business analysis (formerly the `ba` profile): discovery,
> requirements, and story writing, in addition to solution design.

## Codebase Contextualization
- **Always scan existing `force-app/main/default` and project metadata files** before proposing changes.
- Read `.setup-agents/project-knowledge.md` first — it contains architecture decisions, naming conventions, label language, and codebase map.
- If project-knowledge.md is missing or incomplete, ask the user before assuming conventions.
- Reuse existing patterns, utilities, and conventions instead of reinventing them.

## PO/BA User Validation Gate (CRITICAL)
- Product Owner / BA work must validate user stories, definitions, assumptions, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and priority with the user before architecture starts.
- Do not hand work to Architect as ready-for-design while user-facing scope or expected behavior is still ambiguous.
- Record open questions and keep the work in refinement when validation is missing.
- Architect must reject architecture handoff when acceptance criteria, definitions, assumptions, non-goals, or priority are not user-validated.

### ADP Phase 1 — BA + SA Collaborative Gate
- Functional refinement is a **BA + SA joint activity**: the BA owns business intent, the SA validates feasibility against the org, and both sign off before the story is Ready-for-Design.
- A story only clears this gate when the functional probes are answered, acceptance criteria meet the AC quality bar, and an initial ROM has been recorded.
- This BA + SA gate IS the PO/BA validation gate above — run one collaborative sign-off, not two separate validations; it feeds the `ba→architect` handoff.

## Related Prior Work Review (CRITICAL)
- Before refining a story or handing off a tasking decision, read this phase's own context
  (`sf setup-agents workflow context --task <phaseTaskId>`) for its "Related prior work" section —
  up to 5 open stories and 5 accepted decisions from OTHER stories that overlap this one.

# Command Permissions

This file is rendered from the typed runtime permission policy. Profile capabilities provide
task context only; they do not silently elevate command permissions.

Active profile capabilities: deploy, code-analysis, doc-sync, prompt-registry, declare-points, oclif-plugin, org-assessment, story-mapping, adr, decomposition, elements-sync, project-knowledge-bootstrap, story-refinement, audience-tailored-reports, backlog-sync, rom, mobile-appium-testing.

## Capability policy

| Risk | Decision | Representative argv | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------------------|---------|
| read-only | **allow** | `pwd`, `ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `find`, `grep`, `rg`, `jq` | Read and search local files without redirects or shell composition. |
| read-only | **allow** | `git status`, `git diff`, `git log`, `git show`, `git rev-parse`, `git ls-files`, `git config --get` | Inspect the local Git worktree, history, references, and configuration. |
| read-only | **allow** | `npm test`, `npm run <safe-script>`, `yarn test`, `yarn run <safe-script>`, `tsc`, `eslint` | Run existing unit, build, typecheck, and lint scripts without install or fix flags. |
| local-write | **ask** | `mkdir`, `touch`, `cp`, `mv`, `git add`, `git stash`, `git branch`, `git restore`, `git rebase` | Create, change, stage, move, or restore local files or Git state. |
| network-dependency | **ask** | `npm install`, `npm ci`, `yarn install`, `pip install`, `pip3 install`, `npx`, `curl` | Access the network, download executable content, or install dependencies. |
| read-only | **allow** | `sf setup-agents`, `sf sfps-adp` | The plugin's own command surface (task/evidence/workflow tracking) — always safe to run. |
| git-remote-shared | **allow** | `git commit`, `git pull`, `git fetch` | Commit locally, or incorporate remote changes via pull/fetch — scoped to this clone and reversible (revert/reflog), unlike a push or tag that changes shared remote state. |
| git-remote-shared | **ask** | `git checkout`, `git rm`, `git push`, `git tag`, `npm publish`, `npm unpublish` | Change shared Git history/state, publish packages, or incorporate remote changes. |
| git-remote-shared | **ask** | `git push --force`, `git push -f`, `git push --force-with-lease` | Force-pushes, overwriting shared remote history — asks, same as a plain push. |
| destructive | **ask** | `git reset --hard`, `git clean` | Rewrites local history or discards untracked files — reversible via reflog/backup in most cases, so this asks rather than denying outright (user decision, permission-allow-tier-review AC-8). |
| destructive | **deny** | `rm`, `sudo` | Delete local data or escalate privileges. |
| destructive | **deny** | `sf org delete`, `sf org delete scratch`, `sf org delete sandbox`, `sf org delete shape`, `sf org delete snapshot`, `sf env delete scratch`, `sf env delete sandbox`, `sf force org shape delete`, `sf force org snapshot delete`, `sf force org delete`, `sf package version delete`, `sf force package version delete`, `sf org refresh sandbox`, `sf package delete`, `sf force package delete`, `sf package bundle delete` | Delete a scratch org, sandbox, org shape/snapshot, package, or package version — including every verified env:*/force:* alias and colon-joined id for the same underlying command. |
| org-mutate-deploy | **allow** | `sf` | Any other 'sf' command not covered by the explicit deny rules above. |

Commands are parsed as argv. Shell chains, redirects, substitutions, malformed quoting, and
unknown commands fail closed. Substring matches never grant permission.

## Runtime enforcement support

| Runtime | Enforcement | Detail |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| opencode | native-command-policy | Generated native rules deny by default and preserve ask decisions. |
| claude | approval-only | Generated .claude/settings.local.json pre-approves `Bash(sf *)` with no ask tier and denies only the irreversible carve-outs; the PreToolUse hook enforces workflow-gate deny/ask on top. setup-agents cannot express the complete argv policy in CLI flags beyond that. |
| codex | approval-only | Suggest mode retains approval, but setup-agents cannot express the complete argv policy in CLI flags. |
| cursor | unsupported | Cursor print mode has no setup-agents command-policy enforcement channel. |

## Decisions

- **allow**: may run without additional approval.
- **ask**: requires explicit approval scoped to the exact command and target.
- **deny**: must not run. Unknown or unrepresentable operations are denied.

## PreToolUse hook exceptions (subagent-approval-friction)

The Claude Code PreToolUse hook (`.setup-agents/hooks/claude-hook.mjs`) auto-allows four
narrow cases beyond the table above, each keyed off a CLI-established fact, never agent
text, and each fails safe to the pre-existing deny/ask on any ambiguity:

| Case | Condition to auto-allow | Mechanism |
|------|--------------------------|-----------|
| Delete a scratch root | `rm`/`rm -r` target resolves (realpath) inside a path THIS session registered via `sf setup-agents scratch register --path`, unexpired (24h) | `sf setup-agents scratch delete --path <path>` — the hook auto-allow alone cannot bypass the native `Bash(rm *)` deny, so use this command, not a raw `rm` |
| Stop a spawned process | `kill <pid>` targets a pid+start-time THIS session registered via `sf setup-agents scratch register --pid`, unexpired (24h) | `sf setup-agents scratch stop --pid <pid>` |
| Mention a protected path | A Bash command only READS or MENTIONS a protected state/settings path (e.g. inside a quoted `--summary`, or a `grep`) — no real redirect/mutating verb outside quotes | No action needed — already allowed; only a REAL write is denied |
| Docs-only rework | A rejection/correction is docs-only AND a fresh `src/`+`test/` digest still matches the digest recorded when `security-review`/`qa` last passed | Automatic — `workflow run`/`review complete` skip re-opening those two phases and record an audit evidence entry |

Everything else — mandatory gates (`ba→architect`, `document-review→release`), `git push`,
deletes/kills outside an owned scratch root or pid, production deploys, permission/hook
file changes, and bulk state mutation — stays exactly as strict as the table above.

# Scope Assessment & Split Decision

## Goal
Evaluate task scope and complexity before developer handoff. Flag oversized or cross-cutting tasks for split.

## When to Run
REQUIRED before every architect→developer handoff. This ensures cross-cutting work is identified early.

## Step 1 — Measure Scope
Count the affected boundaries:
- How many directories/packages are touched?
- How many object types (Apex, LWC, Flow, metadata, config)?
- Does it cross module boundaries (e.g. force-app + scripts + CI)?

## Step 2 — Complexity Signals
Check for these red flags:
- [ ] Touches 3+ top-level directories → likely cross-cutting
- [ ] Requires changes to both backend (Apex) and frontend (LWC/Aura)
- [ ] Involves both schema changes and code changes
- [ ] Estimated > 3 days solo effort (sizing m or above)
- [ ] Multiple integration points or external system changes

## Step 3 — Split Decision
Based on scope:

**If 2+ red flags are present:**
1. Recommend splitting into child stories.
2. List proposed child tasks with clear boundaries.
3. Record decision: \`sf setup-agents decision add --task <id> --owner architect --title "Split: <reason>" --decision "Split into N child stories" --context "<scope details>" --consequences "Parallel delivery possible" --status accepted\`

**If scope is acceptable (0-1 red flags):**
1. Explicitly document: "Scope assessed — single story acceptable."
2. Record decision: \`sf setup-agents decision add --task <id> --owner architect --title "Scope assessment" --decision "No split needed" --context "<brief justification>" --consequences "Proceed as single story" --status accepted\`

## Step 4 — Record Evidence
\`\`\`bash
sf setup-agents evidence add --task <id> --role architect --type report \\
  --summary "Scope assessment: <N> boundaries, <N> red flags, decision: <split|no-split>"
\`\`\`

## Anti-patterns (DO NOT)
- Do NOT handoff with "gaps: none, risks: none" without running this assessment
- Do NOT skip this for tasks estimated ≥ m (3+ days)
- Do NOT use generic text — always include specific boundary count and decision

## Evidence
```bash
sf setup-agents evidence add --task <id> --role developer --type file --summary "Scope Assessment & Split Decision completed"
```

## Goal
Document a significant architectural decision.

## ADR Template
```markdown
# ADR-NNN: <Title>
```

# Architecture Review

## Goal
Validate that the proposed solution meets non-functional requirements and delegate implementation to the correct domain profile.

## Step 0 — Identify the implementor profile (CRITICAL)
Before closing this phase, read `.setup-agents/config.json` and identify which profile owns implementation:
```bash
cat .setup-agents/config.json | grep -A20 '"profiles"'
```
The implementor is the first active profile that is NOT `pm`, `sa`, `architect`, `qa`, or `release-manager`.
Common values: `cgcloud`, `developer`, `service`, `commerce`, `crma`, etc.
Include the resolved profile in the handoff summary so the pipeline creates the task with the correct role.

## Checklist
- [ ] Scope assessment: run `scope-assessment.md` playbook (REQUIRED for tasks ≥ m)
- [ ] Scalability: handles expected load (1 to N records)
- [ ] Security: sharing model correct, no hardcoded credentials
- [ ] Maintainability: follows existing patterns, no mega-classes
- [ ] Testability: >90% coverage achievable
- [ ] Integration: no tight coupling to external systems
- [ ] Implementor profile identified and declared in handoff

## Steps
1. Read the story and proposed design.
2. Identify the implementor profile (Step 0 above).
3. Walk through the checklist.
4. List any blockers or required changes.
5. Declare delivery estimate (Step 6 below).

## Step 6 — Declare T-Shirt Estimate (REQUIRED before handoff)
Before closing this phase, declare a delivery estimate so benchmarks can track actual vs. baseline:

```bash
# Check if an estimate already exists (idempotent — skip if found)
sf setup-agents workflow benchmark --story <storyId>

# If no estimate exists, declare one:
sf setup-agents workflow estimate \
  --story <storyId> \
  --sizing <xxs|xs|s|m|l|xl|xxl> \
  --solo-days <n> \
  --ai-unguided-days <n> \
  --ai-guided-days <n> \
  --confidence <low|medium|high> \
  --declared-by architect
```

**Sizing scale** — human-equivalent effort days (GH-496):
| Label | Human effort |
|-------|--------------|
| xxs   | trivial, < 4 hours |
| xs    | half-day–1 day (4–8h) |
| s     | 1–2 days |
| m     | 3–5 days (≈ 1 week) |
| l     | 6–8 days |
| xl    | 9–11 days (≈ 1 sprint) |
| xxl   | 12+ days — **split gate** |

> **`xxl` is a split gate, not an estimate.** An XXL story MUST be broken into
> smaller stories (xl or below) before it can be estimated or enter a sprint.
> The estimate path refuses to budget an xxl and emits a "must split" outcome —
> never assign it a day value.

- `--solo-days`: how long a solo developer would take without AI assistance.
- `--ai-unguided-days`: how long with a generic AI assistant (no agent workflow).
- `--ai-guided-days`: how long expected with setup-agents guided workflow (profiles + orchestration). This is the ROI baseline — it becomes the denominator for `vsAiGuidedPct` in the benchmark.
- `--confidence`: your confidence in the estimate (low/medium/high).

> **Backfill:** if the estimate was already recorded without `--ai-guided-days`, re-run the command with only `--story`,
